name: robust_cell_openness
hypothesis: Nonlinear intensive measures of cell openness and lattice shape identify sparse, vacuum-dominated, or highly open structural regimes where linear raw volume-per-atom extrapolates poorly; these regimes should alter formation-energy prediction and may affect hull calibration.
scope: All variable-size periodic cells. Parameters are fixed: log1p(volume/N), covalent-sphere packing using 4*pi*r_cov^3/3, neighbor counts at 3.0 and 6.0 A, sparse indicator E/N<1, cube-root spacing normalized by mean covalent radius, and max/min row-vector length plus mean absolute pairwise lattice cosine.
falsification: Falsified if adaptive formation MAE does not improve over raw30, especially if the extreme sparse-cell errors remain, and if hull logloss also does not improve. A gain confined to the inspected outliers with worse aggregate validation counts as failure.
